placeNote: NY clients read the New York metro (QUESTIONS 210) where a Primary figure gives it: spending scales by the metro's BEA price parity. Rent has no Primary metro figure yet (data.census.gov and the Census API were not reachable), so a NY renter reads New York State's median gross rent and says so. Cash, cards, loans and net worth stay national (no Primary place row). A place row is { field, place, area, factor, source, table, link, year }; a row with its own place (rent) is used as is
leftOut: NY metro median gross rent (ACS B25064 for CBSA 35620): no Primary page reachable (USAFacts says about $1,830 for 2020-2024, Secondary)
Gross rent quartiles: the ACS publishes contract rent quartiles (B25057, B25059), not gross; neither was reachable
Rent by age of householder: no published table (ACS PUMS only)
Cash, cards, student loans and retirement by age (SCF historical tables and Data Interactive): not reachable; the report gives them for all families only
Household income by age (Census H-10 and its percentiles): Secondary
Average card debt by generation (Experian) and student loans by age (FSA portfolio by age, located but not readable): Secondary
CE one-person households by age: no published cross-table; the one-person row is scaled by the age band's ratio to all ages (QUESTIONS 336, batch 46)
CE all consumer units for 2024 (BLS cesan, Dec 19 2025): not reachable; the all-ages total is the 2022-23 average from the NY metro release (QUESTIONS 380)

shapes.note: Income by age is still Secondary (Census H-10), so the all-households median is shaped like spending: times the age band's (and living alone's) CE total over the all-ages total, and for a place by its price parity (no Primary place income row yet)

Cash by age is not reachable (SCF historical tables), so the all-ages median is shaped like spending (cash is spending money): times the age band's (and living alone's) CE total over the all-ages total

Retirement accounts by age are not reachable (SCF historical tables), so the all-ages median among holders is shaped by the age band's median net worth over the all-ages median (the SCF's own age split)
